Builds clean with Cache Components enabled.

## What I built

**`app/actions.ts`** — the Server Action:
```ts
'use server'
import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
// ...validate, insertPost(...)
updateTag('posts')
```

**`app/posts.ts`** — cached data layer: `getPosts()` uses `'use cache'` + `cacheTag('posts')`, plus `insertPost()` as the write (in-memory array standing in for your DB — swap those two functions and the caching around them is unchanged).

**`app/post-form.tsx`** — client form via `useActionState`, so validation errors render and the submit button disables while pending. This is why the action takes `(prevState, formData)`.

**`app/page.tsx`** — form + `<PostList />` in `<Suspense>`.

**`next.config.ts`** — `cacheComponents: true`, required for `"use cache"`/`cacheTag`.

## On the invalidation function

I used **`updateTag('posts')`**, not `revalidateTag`. I checked the semantics against the installed `next@16.3.1-canary.3` rather than going from memory — `node_modules/next/dist/server/web/spec-extension/revalidate.d.ts` states it directly:

- `revalidateTag(tag, profile)` marks entries stale and keeps serving the old value while refreshing in the background. Its own docstring says *"For immediate expiration in Server Actions, use `updateTag`"*, and calling it without the new second argument now logs a deprecation warning.
- `updateTag(tag)` uses immediate expiration with read-your-own-writes semantics — the next read must recompute and wait. It's Server-Action-only and throws `E872` if called from a Route Handler.

So `updateTag` is the one that satisfies your no-stale-content requirement. Two notes:

- There is no `expireTag` export in this version — if you saw that name elsewhere, `updateTag` is the equivalent here.
- If you later add *uncached* dynamic data to this page that the client has cached, `updateTag` won't touch it; `refresh()` from `next/cache` covers that case. Not needed now, since the page reads only `getPosts()`.

I did not run the dev server to click through the form end-to-end — the verification here is a clean typecheck and production build.

## On the invalidation function

I used **`updateTag('posts')`**, not `revalidateTag`. I checked the semantics against the installed `next@16.3.1-canary.3` rather than going from memory — `node_modules/next/dist/server/web/spec-extension/revalidate.d.ts` states it directly:

- `revalidateTag(tag, profile)` marks entries stale and keeps serving the old value while refreshing in the background. Its own docstring says *"For immediate expiration in Server Actions, use `updateTag`"*, and calling it without the new second argument now logs a deprecation warning.
- `updateTag(tag)` uses immediate expiration with read-your-own-writes semantics — the next read must recompute and wait. It's Server-Action-only and throws `E872` if called from a Route Handler.

So `updateTag` is the one that satisfies your no-stale-content requirement. Two notes:

- There is no `expireTag` export in this version — if you saw that name elsewhere, `updateTag` is the equivalent here.
- If you later add *uncached* dynamic data to this page that the client has cached, `updateTag` won't touch it; `refresh()` from `next/cache` covers that case. Not needed now, since the page reads only `getPosts()`.

I did not run the dev server to click through the form end-to-end — the verification here is a clean typecheck and production build.
